text: slope. Together, they widened the gap, opening the small tunnel up to the outside air stone by stone, until David’s face came into view. Pale. Dust-caked. Blood seeping from his temple. But there was a pulse. It fluttered weakly beneath Dwight’s fingers — thready, irregular, but definitely there. Felix threw another stone off to the side, trying to sort out just how bad of an angle David was pinned at. Now that he had a better view, he could spot the edge of a much longer piece than the stones they had been digging at crossing over his collarbone. It seemed to be bracing the worst of the upper pile from digging too sharply into his torso, but there was no way to tell from here how far down it reached. For all he knew, David’s legs could be absolute pulp further down, without this slab protecting them. Some of these stones were insanely heavy and sharp. It was a good thing this larger piece had been preventing those sharp edges from cutting into vital organs. The slab would have taken all that weight and spread it out, instead of letting it stab straight down. Less of a battering and more... Nudging Dwight to the side, Felix crouched to work a hand down along his collarbone, trying to get under the slab. The muscles under his hand were lightly flexing in shallow, sporadic bursts against the weight above. The pressure had been spread out over his entire chest, compressing him down against the sand with every piece that fell from above. The geometry clicked. That slab was at the bottom of the pile. It wasn’t new to the collapse — it has been there from the start. Felix stared at David’s half-buried body, heart thudding, brain kicking into gear. The compression hadn’t just happened at the end — it had been building. For minutes , maybe longer. That stupid, stupid man hadn’t said a word. He’d held it all in. Let it get worse. Let it crush him while they were trying to help. Of course the panic had hit. Of course he had snapped. Anyone would have after that long. “You absolute idiot,” Felix hissed, shoving himself to his feet. He had to get that weight up and off David’s chest. He needed something sturdy. Anything. He spun in place for a moment, doing a rapid inventory of the area around him and coming up empty. His eyes paused on a nearby doorway, catching a flash of movement as Jill lead Nemesis on a wild goose chase in the distance, before refocusing much closer, a spark of an idea forming. “Keep clearing what you can,” he barked to Dwight. “I’ll be right back.” He sprinted for the edge of the Eyrie, boots skidding on broken rubble as he bolted out into the courtyard. His eyes locked onto the small ring of rusted iron fencing around one of the grave plots — nonsensical little monuments the Entity had scattered like décor. They looked sturdy; hopefully it would be enough. He crashed into the closest post, gripped the bars, and wrenched . They didn’t give easily. But he didn’t stop. Anger fueled him. At David. At himself. At the Entity. At the design of this entire place. With a shout and a final kick, a chunk of the wrought iron fencing snapped free with a pained squeal. Felix turned and ran — twisted metal gripped like a weapon — back into the dark. Dwight had stopped trying to clear the top of the pile. Too unstable. Every time he shifted something, it felt like the rest of it wanted to come with. Instead, he’d gone back into his small tunnel, and set himself to widening it. Probably not the smartest idea he had all day, he mused, but they needed to get some kind of space around him and the top kept shifting around too damned much. Maybe from down here, Dwight could get some of the pressure off him so he could breathe easier. He had noted Felix’s unspoken concern almost immediately, and had double checked for himself. David was technically still breathing, if you could call it that. Small, insufficient wisps at far too high of a speed didn’t really instill confidence. But at least David was still trying. Dwight dug his way around the shallower end of the pile, working down past David’s left arm — thankfully not pinned under him — and opening a gap around his side. Thanks to the slab above, he had a nearly clear line down both sides of David’s torso, but couldn’t get much of the weight off without making the upper layers shift threateningly. He followed along the fabric of David’s jacket hem, sweeping away more debris and trying to get at the stones around the large piece pinning his torso in place. Every one that he managed to shift sent small streams of grit raining down around him, making him question every move. He didn’t really feel much like being buried alongside David. Outside the rubble, he could hear Felix storming back in, already calling on him to get out of the way. “Shift! Give me space — I don’t want to accidently hit you!” “Hit me? What are you —” “Get out ! Just MOVE .” Dwight barely managed to push himself backwards along his cramped tunnel before a chunk of metal speared through the space between a few stones. He yelped and yanked his arm out of the way, scampering out of the gap to see Felix trying to pry the stones up with what looked like a busted piece of fencing. He angled the fence piece, one end digging into the rubble while the other rested across a larger chunk.
